chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥusayn, from Mūsā ibn Saʿdān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:
Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “The nose and the mouth do not become junub, because they are flowing passages.”

key_terms.الْأَنْفُ: the nose, mentioned here in relation to ritual purity rulings
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْفَمُ: the mouth, mentioned here in relation to ritual purity rulings
key_terms.سَائِلَانِ: two flowing passages; meaning channels through which things pass
key_terms.لَا يُجْنِبُ: does not become affected by janabah or enter the state of major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: Do the nose and mouth become junub in the rulings of ritual purity?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling related to janabah and ritual purification. It indicates that the nose and mouth are not treated as becoming junub in themselves, because they are passages through which substances flow.
